messages:
James (Customer): Hey team — urgent: our similarity search dropped. We use the same code and model alias `embed-xy-2` but embeddings dims differ by deployment: hosted returns length=1536, our Dedicated returns length=1024, and Private fails with 400 when sending batch >1. Started ~10:15 UTC. Attaching minimal repro and headers below.

James (Customer): curl we used to call Hosted: 
```
curl -s -H \"Authorization: Bearer $HOSTED_TOKEN\" \\n  -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" \\n  -d '{"input": ["hello world"]}' \\n  https://api.redwood-hosted.com/v1/embeddings?model=embed-xy-2
```
Hosted response (trimmed): `{\"embedding\": [ ..., /* 1536 numbers */ ... ] }`

James (Customer): Dedicated call (same client code): 
```
curl -s -H \"Authorization: Bearer $DEDICATED_TOKEN\" \\n  -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" \\n  -d '{"input": ["hello world"]}' \\n  https://dedicated.myorg.redwood.com/v1/embeddings?model=embed-xy-2
```
Dedicated response (trimmed): `{\"embedding\": [ ..., /* 1024 numbers */ ... ] }`

James (Customer): Private behavior: single-item requests succeed (returns 1536) but when we send `input` with 4 items batching we get 400: `Batch size 4 exceeds max_batch 2 for model variant embed-xy-2-quant`. We suspect different quantization or model variant mapping. Also noticed a billing jump for the account yesterday.

SupportBot: Incident created: INC-2026 — \"embed dim mismatch / private batching error\". Notifying on-call.

Maria (Support): Thanks @James — we're looking. Can you paste the exact `request_id` headers from each response and the `X-Model-Version` / `X-Model-Alias` headers if present? Also confirm which SDK/runtime you use and whether you set any custom batching or `max_tokens` flags.

James (Customer): Request ids: Hosted `req_h_01AXYZ`, Dedicated `req_d_0BZXQ`, Private `req_p_3LMNO`. We use our server (node 18) + official redwood-js SDK v0.9. Client config: `batching: auto`, `maxBatchSize: 8`. No special headers normally.

Ashwin (Eng): First-pass hypotheses: 1) Alias `embed-xy-2` maps to different model artifacts in different deployments (e.g., hosted points to model_id `m-1536-abc`, dedicated to `m-1024-def`) 2) Private is routing to a quantized variant with a much lower supported batch size 3) Auth token scopes caused private to hit fallback path returning different variant.

Ashwin (Eng): Steps to validate — run these control-plane commands (replace $TOKEN):
```
# list alias mapping for hosted/dedicated/private (control-plane API)
curl -H \"Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN\" \\n  https://control.redwood.ai/v1/aliases/embed-xy-2
```
Look for `target_model_id`, `variant`, `quantization_profile`. If they differ, that's the root cause.

Maria (Support): Also check the per-deployment model manifest on Dedicated and Private: sometimes a model onboarding script created `embed-xy-2` alias but pointed to a trimmed/quantized artifact in Dedicated. Ask infra to paste manifest lines for the model bundle.

Olivia (SRE): I pulled the Dedicated manifest for the tenant and see `model_id: m-1024-def` and `quantization: int8`. Hosted points to `m-1536-abc` with `fp16`. Private was auto-deployed from a previous import, variant `embed-xy-2-quant` with `max_batch: 2`. So yes, alias divergence.

Olivia (SRE): Root causes we observed in similar incidents: 
- alias drift during manual model swaps 
- import tooling that auto-quantizes on Private deployments 
- retry/ingest middleware that retried non-idempotent calls and spiked billing when dimensions caused re-ingestion

Maria (Support): Immediate mitigation steps for customer: 
1) Temporarily pin client to model version explicit param: `?model=embed-xy-2&model_version=m-1536-abc` for all deployments to enforce parity.
2) For Private, set `batch_size: 1` or `max_batch=1` in client to avoid 400s while we reconcile mapping.
3) Disable client-side retries for embedding requests until idempotency is verified to avoid billing duplication.

James (Customer): Will try pinning version and lowering batch size. One question: how do we find which requests caused the billing spike? We saw a +60% token/embedding unit increase yesterday.

Olivia (SRE): We can correlate by request_ids and timestamps. I recommend exporting usage for your org for the time window and filtering on `endpoint: /v1/embeddings`. Also check for repeated identical payloads (copied request bodies) — that's a sign of retry loops. I'll run a query and paste a short csv.

InfraBot: Export job queued (job_id export-553). ETA ~2m.

Ashwin (Eng): Long-term fixes we should implement on our side: 
- Control-plane validation: block alias update if `target_model` dims/arch differ from previous alias unless force flag set.
- Add `alias:immutable` flag for enterprise tenants to prevent drift.
- Add explicit `X-Model-Version` and `X-Quantization` response headers to make debugging easier.

Maria (Support): For immediate reconciliation, Eng/SRE : can you run a migration to re-point Dedicated alias to `m-1536-abc` and redeploy the Private import pipeline without auto-quantization? If we can't switch the Dedicated model we should notify the customer and suggest fallback to hosted for parity.

Ashwin (Eng): I'll coordinate. Commands I'll run: 
```
# update alias mapping (requires admin scope)
curl -X PATCH -H \"Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN\" \\n  -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" \\n  -d '{"target_model_id":"m-1536-abc"}' \\n  https://control.redwood.ai/v1/aliases/embed-xy-2
```
Then queue a rolling restart of the dedicated model-serving pool and invalidate cache: `POST /v1/serving/pools/<pool>/invalidate?model=embed-xy-2`.

Olivia (SRE): I've run the alias update on Dedicated and kicked a pool restart. Private import pipeline flagged the quantizer step and I disabled it; re-importing now. 

InfraBot: Job `import-embed-xy-2` succeeded.

James (Customer): After your change Dedicated now returns 1536 vectors. Private batch of 4 succeeds too. Confirming similarity search results look back to normal. Huge thanks. :pray: :white_check_mark:

Maria (Support): Great — marking INC-2026 as resolved pending 24h monitoring. We'll keep tracking for any residual billing anomalies.

Olivia (SRE): FYI we found an unrelated token-scope issue that caused Private to route to a fallback variant for some requests (401 in logs when SDK omitted `model:read` scope). We patched error message to be clearer: `401: token missing model:read scope — fell back to quantized-limited-variant`. This should reduce silent fallbacks in future.

Ashwin (Eng): Follow-ups: 
- We'll add an alias-consistency check in the control-plane next sprint.
- Product will provide a guideline on `batch_size` expectations for quantized variants.

James (Customer): Thanks everyone. Please keep me posted if you see any more diffs.

Maria (Support): Noted — we'll email the incident summary and action items. If anything regresses ping this thread or open a new ticket.

SupportBot: Incident INC-2026 closed by Maria (Support) after confirmation from customer.
